title: A wider momentum uncertainty
hook: Change momentum uncertainty and predict minimum position-uncertainty bound.
misconception: minimum position-uncertainty bound doubles when momentum uncertainty doubles, regardless of the stated relationship.
objective: Apply Δx ≥ ħ/(2Δp) to compare minimum position-uncertainty bound when momentum uncertainty changes, under the stated assumptions.

claims.text: With the Heisenberg uncertainty relation for positive uncertainties, Δx ≥ ħ/(2Δp). When momentum uncertainty doubles, minimum position-uncertainty bound becomes ½ times its original value.
claims.source: Idealized model Δx ≥ ħ/(2Δp); scaling exponent -1. Physics and assumptions await independent review.

recall.question: Consider the Heisenberg uncertainty relation for positive uncertainties, with a nonzero initial result. If momentum uncertainty triples from a positive value, what is the multiplier on minimum position-uncertainty bound?
recall.why: Apply Δx ≥ ħ/(2Δp) under the same assumptions: the multiplier is 1/3.
